Which documents are required to apply for residence permit? • Student Residence Permit Application Form (It is created by the system when the application is completed via the e-residence system. The application form is printed out and signed by applicant and / or his / her legal representative.)
• Original and photocopy of the passport or document which is equivalent to passport (Passport or passport replacement of 60 days more period than the requested residence permit must be obtained.)
• Photo (taken in the last six months, fund should be white, biometric and four pieces.)
• Valid Health Insurance (The duration of health insurance should cover the requested residence permit period).
• Declaration of sufficient and regular financial means
• Valid and Accurate Address Statement (If you are staying in a dormitory with an e-signed/signed and sealed/stamped dormitory certificate, if you are staying with rental agreement, notary approved rental agreement)
• Student certificate/Foreign Student Information Form which indicates that they can benefit from the right of studentship

- ##### Which institution gives the residence permit certificate? Which institution gives the residence permit certificate? • Residence permit certificate is issued by General Directorate of Immigration Administration and sent to the addresses of applicants by post (PTT cargo).

- ##### What are valid health insurance types? What are valid health insurance types? • e-Signed/signed and sealed/stamped document received from the Provincial Social Security unitabout benefiting of health services in Turkey within the scope of bilateral social security agreements,
• e-Signed/signed and sealed/stamped authorisation ertificate from Social Security institution,
• e-Signed/signed and sealed/stamped document for application to benefit General Health Insurance (optional insurance) of Social Security institution
• Private Health Insurance,

- ##### Example of residence permit Example of residence permit

- ##### What should the student do if he / she transfers to a university in a different city? What should the student do if he / she transfers to a university in a different city? • If the students transfer to a university, faculty or department in a different city, they must apply for residence permit to Provincial Immigration Administration Directorate where the new University is located within 10 days.

- ##### Can the residence permit be extended if the school is extended? Can the residence permit be extended if the school is extended? • If student can not graduate at normal education period, the residence permit can be extended for maximum of yearly periods and not exceeding the maximum education period.
• However student residence permit cannot be issued after maximum education period.

- ##### What is the ultimate goal of quality assurance system in higher education? What is the ultimate goal of quality assurance system in higher education? To produce qualified graduates who can keep up with the requirements of the era as well as the local/regional context, are equipped with universal qualifications, and meet quality requirements.

- ##### What is the relationship between quality assurance system in Turkish Higher Education areas and international systems? What is the relationship between quality assurance system in Turkish Higher Education areas and international systems? Turkey closely follows international quality assurance systems. The processes and practices are updated regularly in order to keep up with the changing world. Especially ESG (European Quality Assurance Standards and Principles) is taken as a basis in quality assurance processes and studies carried out by THEQC. In this context, THEQC has been granted 5-year membership by ENQA (European Association for Quality Assurance in Higher Education) in 2020. In addition, THEQC has memberships of INQAAHE (International Network for Quality Assurance Agencies in Higher Education), APQN (Asia Pacific Quality Network) and US-based CHEA-CIQG (Council for Higher Education Accreditation - CHEA International Quality Group). Besides these memberships, THEQC applied for EQAR (European Quality Assurance Registration Agency in Higher Education) registration as of 2020.

- ##### How do students participate in quality assurance processes? How do students participate in quality assurance processes? Students participate in quality assurance processes at institutional level or in external evaluation phases. They participate in quality assurance processes at institutional level by providing information, taking part in the internal evaluation process of the higher education institution, and participating in the committees and commissions conducting the quality assurance processes. At the same time, students taking part in evaluation teams appointed by THEQC participate in external evaluation processes. In addition, there is a student member in the composition of THEQC members, which ensures student participation in the decisions issued by the Council. Plus, the Student Commission under THEQC conducts studies for students in the field of quality assurance in higher education.

- ##### What is quality assurance and accreditation? What is quality assurance and accreditation? Quality assurance is planned and systematic activities to ensure that learning and teaching, research and development, and management services carried out in higher education institutions are fulfilled according to national and international quality standards. Accreditation is an external assessment and quality assurance process that measures whether a higher education program meets pre-determined, academic and field-specific standards of national or international independent organizations.

- ##### How are quality assurance processes conducted in the Turkish Higher Education system? How are quality assurance processes conducted in the Turkish Higher Education system? Quality assurance processes in Turkey are carried out by higher education institutions (HEIs), Turkish Higher Education Quality Council (THEQC) and independent accreditation agencies. Establishing and maintaining internal quality assurance systems is in the responsibility of HEIs. Quality evaluations of systems are carried out by THEQC, whilst quality of study programs is assessed by independent accreditation agencies. All national HEIs are required to take part at least once every five years in the Institutional External Evaluation Program carried out by THEQC (www.yokak.gov.tr). This program evaluates HEIs in terms of their quality assurance, learning-teaching, research-development, social contribution and governance systems. Besides, as of 2020, THEQC initiated the Institutional Accreditation Program which will grant 2-year or 5-year institutional accreditation to HEIs in Turkey. Some of the important projects developed to increase input quality of higher education system can be listed as increasing threshold score in higher education admission system, introducing limitation in the order of success in medicine, law, engineering, architecture and teaching programs, initiating base point implementation, increasing acceptance criteria of doctoral programs, inclusion of accredited programs in YKS Higher Education Programs and Quota Guideline where our programs are listed. The accredited programs in the guideline are the ones that have only been assessed by the accreditation agencies having THEQC’s authorization (national agencies) or recognition (international agencies).

- ##### What are the duties and responsibilities of Turkish Higher Education Quality Council? What are the duties and responsibilities of Turkish Higher Education Quality Council? Turkish Higher Education Quality Council started its activities in 2015. THEQC has three main duties. The first is to carry out external evaluations of higher education institutions; the second is to carry out the recognition (national) and authorization (international) processes of national or international accreditation agencies operating in Turkey for program accreditation. Ensuring internalization and dissemination of quality assurance culture in higher education institutions is the third duty of THEQC.

- ##### What does accredited program mean? How many accredited programs are available in Turkey? What does accredited program mean? How many accredited programs are available in Turkey? A program with accreditation guarantees that targeted program outputs and program objectives have been reached. As of 2020, there are 796 programs accredited by THEQC authorized (national) or recognized (international) accreditation agencies in Turkey. These programs are included in YKS Higher Education Programs and Quota Guideline. Accredited programs are in the fields of pharmacy, science-literature, health sciences, architecture, engineering, psychology, medicine, veterinary medicine and educational sciences. The list of accreditation agencies authorized/recognized by THEQC can be found on the official website of THEQC (www.yokak.gov.tr).

- ##### What is Institutional External Evaluation Program? What is Institutional External Evaluation Program? THEQC evaluates the quality levels of HEIs via the Institutional External Evaluation Program. In Turkey, 160 HEIs were subject to external evaluation between the years of 2016 and 2019. The evaluations are carried out by independent evaluation teams appointed by THEQC. In evaluation teams; academicians, administrative staff and students are included. As a result of the evaluations, an institutional feedback report is prepared for each institution evaluated, and shared with public. In addition, the list of evaluated institutions is included in the YKS Higher Education Programs and Quota Guideline.

- ##### What are the Unimpeded University Awards? What are the Unimpeded University Awards? In order to determine the activities carried out in order to ensure full, effective and equal participation of persons with disabilities within the university campus borders and for rewarding those who are successful, and also for creating public awareness, universities are awarded Unimpeded University Awards. Scope of Unimpeded University Awards given in categories of Unimpeded University Flag and Unimpeded University Program Medal have been extended by adding Disabled Friendly Individual Awards for 2019-2020 academic year.

- ##### What is Qualified Research Assistant Training Program in Fields which Turkey is in need of?: What is Qualified Research Assistant Training Program in Fields which Turkey is in need of?: **Priority Field Research Assistant Program**, is a scholarship program developed for the goal of raising qualified research assistants in the branches determined primarily by Council of Higher Education, in economic, cultural and scientific fields which Turkey is in need of.
Each year, up to twenty per cent of additional assignment permits determined for faculty members staff other than teaching staff are allocated to higher education institutions under our Presidency in the field of Priority Research Assistants for the purpose of post graduate education. Program applications are made to Presidency of Council of Higher Education by higher education institutions for designated priority branches. After the applications are assessed by CoHE, appropriate universities and staff numbers are notified to relevant universities.

- ##### What is Universal Academician Educating Scholarship Program? What is Universal Academician Educating Scholarship Program? **International Research Scholarship for Research Assistants (IRS),** International Research Scholarship for Research Assistants is a scholarship for expenses of research assistants who are at thesis stage of doctoral education in state universities for making researches abroad about their thesis for a period of at least six months and a maximum of one year

- ##### What is Regional Development Oriented Mission Differentiation and Specialization Program? What is Regional Development Oriented Mission Differentiation and Specialization Program? It is a program aimed at supporting regional activities of 10 selected universities (among universities established in 2006 and later) in order to increase their contributions to the region and to encourage their specialization in certain areas. Financial support is provided for pilot universities which are eligible to be supported for the planned activities. Pilot universities and fields are as follows:
- Bingöl University; Agriculture and basin based development,
- Burdur Mehmet Akif Ersoy University; Livestock,
- Düzce University; Health and environment,
- Kırsehir Ahi Evran University; Agriculture and geothermal,
- Uşak University; Textile, leather and ceramic,
- Aksaray University; Sports and health,
- Kastamonu University; Forestry and Natural Tourism,
- Muş Alpaslan University; Livestock,
- Recep Tayyip Erdogan University; Tea,
Siirt University; Agriculture and livestock

- ##### What is Research-Oriented Mission Differentiation and Specialization Program (Research Universities)? What is Research-Oriented Mission Differentiation and Specialization Program (Research Universities)? It is a program which aims to gain a more competitive structure in the global sense by differentiating missions of 10 Research and 5 candidate Research Universities which are selected among well established Universities. Research Universities:
1. Ankara University
2. Bogazici University
3. Erciyes University
4. Gazi University
5. Gebze Teknik University
6. Hacettepe University
7. Istanbul University
8. Istanbul University-Cerrahpaşa
9. Istanbul Teknik University
10. Izmir Institute of Technology
11. Middle East Technical University

- ##### What is Qualified Undergraduate Student Training Project? What is Qualified Undergraduate Student Training Project? In our Higher Education System, it is important for our country to increase the quality at all levels and in relation to some programmes in the areas designated by CoHE (some programs in the faculties of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries). It is a project to grant scholarships to students enrolled in undergraduate programs in higher education institutions.

- ##### What is Ultimate Success Class? What is Ultimate Success Class? Among the students who are eligible to receive scholarships in Biology-Physics-Chemistry-Mathematics programs within the scope of scholarships given for training of qualified undergraduate students, CoHE-TEBIP (CoHE Basic Science Programs) classes are created for the 30 most successful students in each of these field programs. CoHE TEBIP (Basic Science Program) students are trained as special students in ultimate success classes created within Istanbul University. In diplomas of these students'; “Completed Basic Science Program at Istanbul University in the Ultimate Success Class” phrase will be included.

- ##### What is 7 + 1 project in Science and Engineering Field? What is 7 + 1 project in Science and Engineering Field? It is a project for paying the fees of science and engineering sciences students, in undergraduate level during their mandatory practical training at one semester in the last year of their education in private sector enterprises, technoparks, research infrastructures, R & D Centers and industrial institutions as a practical training fee from the Unemployment Insurance Fund under the Unemployment Insurance Act.

- ##### What is CoHE Foreign Language Education Scholarship? What is CoHE Foreign Language Education Scholarship? **CoHE Foreign Language Education Scholarship,** allows faculty members with PhD degree whose foreign language levels are at a certain level and is ready to be developed to attend a foreign language course abroad.
Within the scope of this Program, faculty members who have Ph.D. degrees in public universities are evaluated by CoHE. For the first time, the applications of the academicians who applied for the 2018-2019 academic year were evaluated and the application of forty faculty members were found appropriate. Scholars will be participating in English, German and French language schools in UK, USA, Canada, Malta, Germany, France, in order to develop their foreign language levels.
Language education of scholars will be performed within two to six months. In the scope of the Program, scholarships are provided to relevant scholars.

- ##### What are the Scholarships given by CoHE to International Students? What are the Scholarships given by CoHE to International Students? Council of Higher Education gives scholarships to students from countries which CoHE have signed cooperation protocol or a memorandum of understanding, or students other than Turkish Nationality who are placed in state higher education institutions, to meet their undergraduate and graduate tuition fees, Turkish language education expenses, general health insurance premiums and dormitory fees Distribution of scholarships to international students according to countries; Kosovo: % 41 Bangladesh: % 7 Pakistan: % 22 Palestine: % 6 Rwanda: % 9 Macedonia: %4 Albania: % 8 Ukraine: %3 Top five universities offering the most international student scholarships: Trakya University, Düzce University, Tekirdağ Namık Kemal University, Kastamonu University, Çukurova University, Erciyes University

- ##### What Is CoHE Scholarship Awarded To Foreign Students?
- It is a scholarship program awarded to foreign students who come from the countries where Council of Higher Education signed a protocol and who are placed in State Higher Education Institutions.
- Scholarships are awarded to foreign students who are placed by CoHE in a higher education program.
- Enrollments begin and end according to academic calendar.

- ##### What Are The Supports Offered To Foreign Students By CoHE Scholarship?
- **800 TL** Scholarship Fee to undergraduate students **, 1400 TL** to graduate students
- Undergraduate and graduate tuition fee
- Turkish language tuition costs for non-Turkish scholars
- Health insurance
- Accommodation in dormitories of Institution of Credit and Dormitories

- ##### Which countries benefit from CoHE scholarship awarded to foreign students as of 2018-2019 academic year? Albania, Bangladesh, Palestine, Kosovo, Macedonia, Pakistan (Azad Kashmir region), Rwanda and Ukraine.

- ##### Who Can Apply To CoHE Scholarship Awarded To Foreign Students?
- Foreign students who are coming from countries where CoHE signed a protocol

- ##### What is a Turcology Scholarship? What is a Turcology Scholarship? Provided that the countries where the Council of Higher Education has signed cooperation act and / or a memorandum of understanding have priority, this is a scholarship which started for the first time in the 2017-2018 academic year for the undergraduate students who are studying in Turkish Language and Literature, Turcology and Turkish Language programs of foreign countries and higher education institutions to be determined by the Council of Higher Education.

- ##### What is CoHE Turcology Scholarship? These are scholarships awarded to undergraduate students who are studying in Turkish Language and Literature, Turkology and Turkish Language programs of higher education institutions to be determined by CoHE. For these scholarships, the countries that signed protocol with CoHE will be given priority.

- ##### Who Can Apply to CoHE Turcology Scholarship? In foreign countries and higher education institutions determined by CoHE, students studying in Turkish Language and Literature, Turkology and Turkish Language Programs can apply. They must meet the following requirements:
1. a) To be ranked in the first 10 of the program for the students who will start preparatory or first grade in higher education institution,
2. b) For students in the second semester of the first class, having a high GPA, i.e. in the top 10 students in the classroom,
3. c) For students studying in intermediate classes; having no failed lessons from the previous year; and having a high GPA of previous year i.e; being in top 10 students in the class.

- ##### How are the course credits determined at universities in Turkey? How are the course credits determined at universities in Turkey? Since 2011, European Credit Transfer System ECTS/ECTS system is legally used in determining course credits in all universities in Turkey. ECTS is a student-centered credit system based on the study load of the student. ECTS credits are based on competencies of the students in a course and are calculated according to study load of students to gain these competencies. Most universities in Turkey have adapted their own credit and grading systems to ECTS principles. Therefore, student-centered education in universities is of considerable importance.

- ##### What is the Bologna Process? What is the Bologna Process? It is a process prepared to create a Higher Education Area in Europe. Process aims to develop academic standards among member countries in higher education. It aims to reduce differences between education systems in member countries. The process is unlike usual agreements. Because there are no agreements, protocols, etc. between participating States. Since they participate in their own requests, implementing achievements and objectives in the process is at the discretion of States. In other words, decisions taken in the Bologna Process have no binding effect on the states. In Higher Education Area to be established within the framework of Bologna Process, nationals of Member States will be able to travel freely and easily to benefit from academic careers or higher education. Another aim of the process is to make education systems and education-related business areas in member countries attractive. Although the aim is to provide high education unity, the situation that the process never wants is a uniform higher education program or system. Process is based on securing differences of original education systems in the countries and establishing a balance between these differences and creation of unity.

- ##### Is Turkey involved in Bologna process, namely European Higher Education area? Is Turkey involved in Bologna process, namely European Higher Education area? With inclusion of Turkey in Bologna process in 2001, quality assurance in Turkish Higher Education was placed in a more prioritized order. However, support and activities related to the Bologna reforms gained momentum especially after 2005. Today , Turkey with more than 7 million students has the largest student population in European Higher Education Area and is one of the leading practitioners of Bologna reforms.

- ##### What is ECTS? **What is ECTS?**
ECTS credits are value based on the study load, which cover the complete study of the student (theoretical course, practice, seminar, individual study, exams, assignments, etc.) in order to successfully complete a course. One academic year corresponds to 60 ECTS credits. Equivalent to this credit, student study load is projected between 1500-1800 hours. 1 ECTS corresponds to 25-30 hours of study load.

- ##### What are the documents required for the short term residence permit applications of students coming within Erasmus program? What are the documents required for the short term residence permit applications of students coming within Erasmus program? • Health insurance
• Student certificate showing that the student is an exchange student
• Valid passport
• Photo
• Address statement

- ##### What types of health insurance are available for Erasmus students? What types of health insurance are available for Erasmus students? For the health insurance requirement of the documents required for residence permit, one of the following is deemed sufficient:
• Within the scope of bilateral social security contracts; document indicating to benefit from health services in Turkey,
• Provision certificate taken from Social Security Institution,
• The document related to application to Social Security Institution for general health insurance,
• Health insurance policies made by foreign students in their own countries (provided that they comply with the minimum policy content in our country and approved by notaries or universities).
• Private Health Insurance Policies

- ##### What is ECTS for? What is ECTS for? ECTS credits are based on competencies of the students in a course and are calculated according to study load of students to gain these competencies. Therefore, since higher education systems of countries are different, ECTS is used to ensure mobility and recognition. Originally considered for credit transfer, this system is also used as a corporate, regional, national and European level credit collection system.

- ##### How is Turkey's Bologna success status? How is Turkey's Bologna success status? Reports are published by European Commission on Evaluation of Higher Education of the Member States every two to three years. In Bologna process implementation report of European Higher Education Area of the year 2018, Turkey received 5 full points in ECTS implementations, Diploma Supplement and Competencies.

- ##### How many ECTS credits should I get at higher education degrees? How many ECTS credits should I get at higher education degrees? 120 ECTS at the undergraduate level, 240 ECTS at Bachelor's level, 120 ECTS at Master's level and 240 ECTS at doctoral level are expected to be collected.

- ##### How can a person who wants to benefit from Mevlana Exchange Program and who has the prerequisites can apply? Students may apply to Mevlana Exchange Program Coordinatorship of his/her Higher Education Institution by filling out forms at http://www.yok.gov.tr/web/mevlana. Faculty members may also apply to the relevant Mevlana Exchange Program Coordinator.

- ##### How can students who benefit from Mevlana Exchange Program meet their housing needs? Within the scope of the program, they can apply to take advantage of dormitories of the Credit Dormitories Institution by contacting the Mevlana Coordinatorship of the university.

- ##### How many times and how long can students benefit from Mevlana exchange program? Students can benefit from Mevlana Exchange Program for at least 1 and a maximum of 2 semesters.

- ##### How many times and how long can lecturers benefit from Mevlana Exchange Program? They can benefit at least for 1 week and a maximum of 3 months in one academic year. Academic activities should be at least 6 hours per week as part of mobility of faculty members. Academic activities such as lectures, seminars, panels or conferences are assessed in this context.

- ##### Does a student who wants to benefit from the Mevlana Exchange Program pay tuition fees for the institution he/she goes to? Students only continue to pay the contribution or tuition fee to the higher education institution where their registry is located during the period during Mevlana Exchange Program. They do not pay any tuition fees to Higher Education Institution to go.

- ##### Will the students who participate in the program lose any semester? Which courses will be considered equivalent to the courses taken by students who are enrolled in Mevlana Exchange Program and who are educated in another country abroad are determined in the learning protocol clearly. In other words, student does not lose any semester when he returns to his country.

- ##### Will the scholarships and credits of students who receive scholarships within the scope of Mevlana Exchange Program be cut off? Other scholarships and credits received by the students participating in Mevlana Exchange Program continue during the period they study. They continue to pay contributions or tuition fees to their institutions and do not pay tuition fees to Higher Education Institution.

- ##### Where can we learn more about Mevlana Exchange Program?
- You can contact the Mevlana Exchange Program Coordinatorship of the higher education institution that you are a student of or you are working at.
- Or you can get information, documents or necessary documents from http://www.yok.gov.tr/web/mevlana web adress, YÖK Mevlana Exchange Program Coordinatorship.

- ##### Which countries and departments can exchange students and instructors? Within the scope of the program, higher education institutions, departments, durations and classes which implement exchange program vary according to Mevlana Protocols signed by Council of Higher Education and countries and departments Council of Higher Education has prioritized. In this context, it is necessary to contact the Mevlana Exchange Program Coordination Office of the higher education institution in which the student is registered or where lecturer is employed.

- ##### What is Mevlana Exchange Program?
- It is a student and instructor exchange program between higher education institutions in Turkey and higher education institutions abroad.

- ##### What is Project-Based International Exchange Program? What is Project-Based International Exchange Program? Mevlana Exchange Program continues to be carried out in 2 ways, after academic year 2016-2017; as "country/field oriented" and "Project based International Exchange Program". In addition, in the scope of call initiated in 2017-2018 academic year for project-based international exchange program, which is based on mobility of graduate students and lecturers between Pakistan and Turkey, PAK-TURK projects are started to be supported by CoHE.

- ##### Who can participate in the Mevlana Exchange Program?
- Students in undergraduate, graduate, postgraduate and doctoral students enrolled in formal education programs in all higher education institutions in Turkey can participate in the course of Mevlana Exchange Program,
- In addition, faculty members who work in domestic and overseas higher education institutions can participate.

- ##### What are the application requirements to participate in Mevlana Exchange Program as a student?
- To be a pre-graduate, undergraduate, graduate or doctoral student enrolled in the higher education programs.
- General academic GPA of undergraduate and undergraduate students should be at least 2.5 out of 4,
- General academic GPA of graduate and doctoral students should be at least 3 out of 4,
- Should have % 50 language score +% 50 grade averages.

- ##### What are the application requirements to participate in Mevlana Exchange Program as an instructor (teacher)? Given priority to specific situations such as the educational language of the higher education institution, the language of instruction and the level of knowledge of this language. In exchange, faculty members who have not previously been involved in exchange activities are given priority.

title: Türkiye Scholarships FAQ - Residence and Immigration
text:
After an online application is made through e-ikamet.goc.gov.tr, you must visit the Provincial Directorate of Migration Management in the province where the university is located on the day of appointment, together with the required documents.

After students complete their applications on e-ikamet.goc.gov.tr, the required documents are specified on their application form. It is also located in the requested documents section on the e-residence system screen. Detailed information about the documents can also be obtained by calling YİMER – 157.

You can get information by going to
the Provincial Migration Administration Directorate in the province where your
university is located or by calling YİMER -157.

Extension applications can be made
from 60 days before the expiration of the residence permit and under any
circumstances must be made before the expiration of the residence permit.
Applications for renewal of residence permits are made to through the
Provincial Directorate of Migration Management in the province where the
university is located, together with the required documents, by making an
appointment at e-ikamet.gov.tr.

Your application will not be
processed. If your residence permit is still valid, you will be able to make a
new appointment. However, if your residence permit has expired, you will be in
violation of residence.

The YTB cannot residence book fee
(document fee) payments made by our students during the residence extension
application.

A residence permit application
document is issued by the Provincial Directorate of Migration Management on the
day of the appointment of our students who have applied. In order to leave the
country, this document must be approved by the Provincial Directorate of
Migration Management. The approved copy of the application document provides
our students with the right to exit and enter the country, provided that they
return within a period of 15 days.

According to the law, student
residence permit applications can only be submitted to the Provincial Migration
Administration Directorates in the province where the university is located. A
student residence permit application cannot be submitted to the Provincial
Directorate of Migration Management in a different province.

Provincial Migration Administration
Directorates may allow up to 30 days to complete the missing documents. If the
missing documents are not completed and delivered to the Provincial Migration
Administration Directorate on time, your application will be removed from
processing.

According to the law, a residence
extension application cannot be made with an expired passport.

According to the law, residence
permit applications cannot be received abroad. Students whose residence permit
expires while they are abroad will be able to enter country according to the
visa regime between the two countries.

You have to visit the Provincial Directorate of Migration Management in the province where your university is located and apply for your duplicate YU numbers to be combined.

title: Work Permit Evaluation Criteria - Ministry of Labour
text:
# Work Permit Evaluation Criteria

##### A. GENERAL EVALUATION CRITERIA

**1. Employment criteria**

1.1. In workplaces subject to the balance sheet basis procedure, for each foreigner for whom a work permit application is made, it is essential to employ at least five Turkish citizens in the workplace where the foreigner will be working.

1.2. Workplaces with net sales of 50,000,000 Turkish Liras or more in the last year, will be exempt from the employment criteria for up to five foreigners.

**2. Financial eligibility criteria**

2.1. For work permit applications made for foreigners to be employed in newly established workplaces (established in the most recent financial year and not yet having prepared a year-end balance sheet and annual income statement), the workplace must have a paid-in capital of at least 500,000 TL.

2.2. For work permit applications made for foreigners to be employed in workplaces operating under the balance sheet basis method (established in a year prior to the current financial year and having prepared at least one year-end balance sheet and annual income statement), the workplace must have either a paid-in capital of at least 500,000 TL, net sales of at least 8,000,000 TL, or exports of at least 150,000 USD.

2.3. For work permit applications made by general partnerships established by workplaces subject to the balance sheet basis method, it is required that at least one partner has either a paid-in capital of at least 500,000 TL, net sales of at least 8,000,000 TL, or exports of at least 150,000 USD.

**3. Salary criteria**

3.1. The remuneration of the foreigner must be at least as follows, takin into account the current gross minimum wage at the time of the work permit application date:

a) Five times the minimum wage for senior executives and pilots,

b) Four times the minimum wage for engineers and architects,

c) Three times the minimum wage for other managers,

d) Twice the minimum wage for those employed in jobs requiring expertise and mastery,

e) The minimum wage for foreigners employed in domestic work and other professions/jobs.

**4. Exceptions to employment and financial eligibility criteria**

4.1 For applications for a domestic work permit submitted on behalf of foreigners who, as of the date of the work permit application, have legally resided in Türkiye for at least one year within the preceding three years under a work permit, residence permit, or international protection status, it is a fundamental principle that the employment and financial eligibility criteria shall not be applied. This exemption is limited to a maximum of three foreigners falling within this category. *(Effective as of August 3, 2026.)*

4.2. It is essential that the number of foreigners working with a work permit in workplaces under the first paragraph does not exceed the number of Turkish citizens employed in the same workplace.

4.3. Provided that the relevant legislation provisions for foreigners under international protection are reserved, if more than three foreigners meeting the conditions in the first paragraph are to work in the same workplace, the evaluation of work permit applications for the fourth and subsequent foreign employees must meet the employment and financial eligibility criteria for each foreigner employed in the workplace.

##### B. EVALUATION CRITERIA PECULIAR TO INDUSTRY, PROFESSION, OR JOB

**1. Information technology industry**

1.1. Employment and financial eligibility criteria will not be applied for work permit applications regarding jobs, professions, or positions requiring expertise, such as software development, database expertise, mobile software expertise, system network and security expertise, and enterprise architecture expertise for the businesses operating in the information technology industry.

1.2. In workplaces operating outside the information technology industry, the employment and financial eligibility criteria will not be applied for work permit applications regarding jobs, professions, or positions requiring expertise, limited to a maximum of two foreigners.

**2. Education**

2.1. In educational institutions, obtaining a pre-permit from the Ministry of National Education or the Council of Higher Education is mandatory for the evaluation work permit applications for foreigners working in professions and positions requiring professional qualifications.

2.2. The work permit applications made on behalf of foreign teaching staff for whom pre-permit has been granted by the Council of Higher Education, the evaluation criteria will not be applied as outlined in the Law No. 6735 on International Labour Force, Article 8, paragraphs three and four.

2.3. Subject to the provisions of international agreements, the employment and financial criteria will not be applied for work permit applications regarding foreigners working in jobs or professions requiring pre-permit according to Article 29 of the Regulation on Private Educational Institutions of the Ministry of National Education.

**3. Domestic work**

3.1. In the domestic work industry, the employment of foreigners is based on the care of the children, elderly, disabled and sick.

3.2. In the domestic work industry:

a) For childcare:

1. If the parents are married, the child's mother or father,
2. If the parents are divorced, the parent with the custody of the child,
3. The person who adopts the child,
4. If the child is under guardianship, the child's legal guardian,
5. The person with the status of a foster mother or foster father within the foster family program,
6. The mother of a child born outside of marriage or the father, who has legally acknowledged that child,

b) For the care of the elderly, disabled, and sick:

1. The disabled, sick, or elderly person themselves,
2. The first or second-degree relatives of the disabled, sick, or elderly person,
3. The guardian of the disabled, sick, or elderly person, if they are under guardianship, or their first or second degree relatives with the consent of the guardian may apply for a work permit.

3.3. In the evaluation of work permit applications, the following situations will be taken into account:

a) The health condition and age of the person to be cared for,

b) Education, professional experience, level of proficiency in the Turkish language, residency or work history in Türkiye, marital status, and age of the foreigner providing car,

c) Other factors indicating the peculiar nature of the tasks for this job,

ç) The socio-economic status of the employer, including their assets, and regular monthly income.

3.4. In domestic work, the person to be cared, or their second-degree (including) blood or in-law relatives who will support them, must have sufficient, continuous, and regular income, as documented by the relevant institutions and organizations. If the person to be cared for or accompanied has no second-degree (including) blood or in-law relatives, other family members wishing to help providing the care must submit a document proving sufficient, continuous, and regular income from the relevant institutions, as well as a notarized commitment to support the care from the employer.

3.5. In domestic work, if a work permit holder, who obtained this permit through an overseas application, would like to apply for another work permit to work for a new employer within six months of the current permit start date, it will be refused, except in cases of force majeure.

**4. Aviation industry**

4.1. Work permit applications for foreigners, who work as senior executives or in specialist positions for the foreign flag carrier airlines’ Türkiye branches, will not be subject to employment and financial eligibility criteria.

**5. High-tech industry**

5.1. For qualified investments that are committed to making a significant contribution to the national economy or creating a high number of jobs, or in cases where there is a need for qualified workforce due to the nature of the job and the unavailability of Turkish citizens with the same qualifications, work permit applications may be exempt from the general evaluation criteria, subject to approval by the Directorate General of International Labour Force.

5.2. For foreigners working as R&D, innovation, and design personnel in companies with R&D or design center certificates under Law No. 5746 on the Support of Research, Development, and Design Activities, and for foreigners working in technology development zones under Law No. 4691 on Technology Development Zones, the approval of the Ministry of Industry and Technology is required. Employment and financial eligibility criteria will not applied in the evaluation of work permit applications in this context.

**6. Public projects**

6.1. In cases where bilateral or multilateral agreements to which Türkiye is a party contain provisions or for foreigners working on projects implemented in Türkiye under such agreements, work permit applications will not be subject to employment and financial eligibility criteria.

6.2. For foreigners to be employed by companies that have contracts or agreements with public institutions and organizations for the supply of goods and services, or by subcontractors working in these projects, the evaluation of work permit applications will not be subject to employment and financial eligibility criteria.

**7. Health industry**

7.1. For foreigners applying for work permits to work in professions requiring professional qualification in health institutions, pre-permit from the Ministry of Health is mandatory.

7.2. In the health industry, for foreigners to work in public institutions in professions requiring professional qualifications, work permit applications will not be subject to employment, salary, or financial eligibility criteria.

**8. Tourism industry**

8.1. For foreigners to be employed in jobs requiring expertise and mastery in tourism industry establishments:

a) Tourism businesses certified by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism,

b) Restaurants operating under a contract at the same address as the tourism business certified by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism,

c) Tourism animation and event management companies operating under a contract with tourism businesses certified by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism,

ç) Hammams, saunas, etc. operating under a contract at the same address as a tourism business certified by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism,

d) Hammams and saunas in a cooperation agreement with businesses holding a tourism agency certificate,

e) Thermal hotels with permit of operation from official authorities, Work permit applications for foreigners from these establishments will not be subject to the employment criteria, provided that at least ten Turkish citizens are employed.

8.2. The work permit applications for jobs requiring expertise and mastery as mentioned in the first paragraph, such as masseurs, masseuses, SPA therapists, and other similar roles, the workplace must be;

a) A tourism business certified by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism that can prove it has a massage salon, or the establishment or a thermal hotel with a permit of operation from the relevant authorities,

b) A massage salon operating under a contract at the same address as a business which is tourism business certified by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism,

c) A hamam or sauna facility which has a contract with a travel agency certificate owning business,

ç) A sports center certified by official authorities employing at least twenty Turkish citizens,

Work permit applications for foreigners to work in jobs requiring expertise and mastery such as masseurs, masseuses, and SPA therapists will be evaluated negatively if the business does not meet the above requirements (a), (b), (c), and (ç).

8.3. In the context of paragraphs 1 and 2, the maximum number of foreigners allowed to work at a business will be determined by the financial and physical capacity of the establishment.

8.4. Work permit applications for foreigners employed in businesses (e.g., hairdressers, jewelers, leather, carpet, textile sales, etc.) operating under a contract at a tourism business certified business by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism Tourism will be evaluated based on an exemption from employment and financial eligibility criteria, but only for a maximum of two foreigners.

8.5. For work permit applications made from within Türkiye for foreigners to work in health tourism activities at travel agencies certified by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism and authorized intermediary organizations by the Ministry of Health, employment and financial eligibility criteria will not be applied for a maximum of five foreigners.

8.6 In enterprises operating in the accommodation sector within the tourism industry, applications for work permits for positions that do not require expertise or mastery shall be evaluated based on the criteria specified in Article 1 titled “Employment Criteria” of Section A, taking into account the number of Turkish citizens employed by the enterprise across Türkiye.

8.7 In enterprises covered under the sixth paragraph, if there is a requirement for additional foreign employment for positions that do not require expertise or mastery, applications for one additional foreign employee for every five Turkish citizens employed at the relevant workplace (on a branch basis) shall be evaluated as exempt from Article 1 titled “Employment Criteria” of Section A. (Effective as of March 11,2026)

**9. Foreign students**

9.1. Foreign students who are enrolled in associate and undergraduate degree programs at a higher education institution in Türkiye can work part-time after completing their first year of study.

9.2. Work permit applications for graduate students enrolled in formal education programs will not be subject to the limitations mentioned in the first paragraph.

9.3. The status of the foreigner as a student will be verified based on the records of the Council of Higher Education (Yükseköğretim Kurulu - YÖK).

9.4. Work permit applications for foreign students wishing to work in jobs unrelated to their field of study in entertainment or domestic work industry will be evaluated negatively.

9.5. In evaluating work permit applications for foreign students enrolled in associate and undergraduate degree programs, factors such as the city in which the student is studying will be considered.

9.6. For foreign students studying under the Türkiye Scholarships Program (Türkiye Bursları), the opinion of the Presidency for Turks Abroad and Related Communities (Yurtdışı Türkler ve Akraba Topluluklar Başkanlığı) will be sought in evaluating work permit applications.

9.7. For foreign students benefiting from the YÖK Scholarship Program, work permit applications made during their studies or after graduation will be evaluated with input from the Council of Higher Education (YÖK).

**10. Livestock sector**

10.1. In the evaluation of work permit applications for shepherds/herd managers to be employed in livestock enterprises in the livestock sector and registered in the Animal Information System with cattle or ovine animals

a) Ovine livestock enterprise must have at least 200 ovine animals, or

b) Beef cattle livestock enterprise must have at least 100 cattle, or

c) Dairy farming enterprise must have at least 50 cattle, or

ç) Mixed (beef cattle and dairy) livestock enterprises must have at least 75 cattle.

10.2. Work permits could be issued for up to three foreign workers without applying the employment criteria in the same livestock enterprise. Also, in each livestock enterprise, one shepherd/livestock caretaker shall be employed for every 200 ovine livestock; in a beef cattle enterprise, for every 100 cattle; in a dairy cattle enterprise, for every 50 cattle; and in a mixed (beef cattle and dairy) cattle enterprise, for every 75 cattle.

10.3. In the evaluation of applications made within the scope of the first and second paragraphs, the opinion of the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry shall be obtained.

10.4. Regarding foreign workers employed under a work permit issued based on an overseas/abroad application in the livestock sector, applications for a new work permit made domestically within six months from the start date of the permit to work for another employer shall be assessed negatively, except in cases of force majeure.

10.5 In livestock enterprises that provide the animal assets covered under this paragraph, it is essential that the financial eligibility criteria shall not be applied. (Effective as of March 11,2026)

**10. A. Manufacturing Sector**

Until 31 December 2027, applications for work permits submitted for one additional foreigner for every five Turkish citizens employed at an establishment operating in the manufacturing sector, calculated on a workplace (branch) basis, shall be assessed without the application of the “Employment Criteria” set forth in Article 1 of Section A. *(Effective as of August 3, 2026.)*

**10.B. Poultry Farming Sector**

Until 31 December 2027, applications for work permits submitted for one additional foreigner for every five Turkish citizens employed at an establishment operating in the poultry farming sector, calculated on a workplace (branch) basis, to be employed in occupations such as animal caretaker, poultry house maintenance worker, and similar positions, shall be assessed without the application of the “Employment Criteria” set forth in Article 1 of Section A.

Furthermore, for workplaces employing fewer than five Turkish citizens, applications for in-country work permits shall, as a matter of principle, be assessed without the application of the employment and financial eligibility criteria for up to two foreigners, provided that the number of foreigners employed under this provision does not exceed the number of Turkish citizens employed. *(Effective as of August 3, 2026.)*

**10.C. Recycling Sector**

Until 31 December 2027, applications for work permits submitted for one additional foreigner for every five Turkish citizens employed at an establishment operating in the waste collection, recovery, and disposal activities sector, calculated on a workplace (branch) basis, to be employed in occupations such as waste collector, recycling worker, and similar positions, shall be assessed without the application of the “Employment Criteria” set forth in Article 1 of Section A.

Furthermore, for workplaces employing fewer than five Turkish citizens, applications for in-country work permits shall, as a matter of principle, be assessed without the application of the employment and financial eligibility criteria for up to two foreigners, provided that the number of foreigners employed under this provision does not exceed the number of Turkish citizens employed. *(Effective as of August 3, 2026.)*

**11. Cases general evaluation criteria applied**

11.1. In cases where no specific evaluation criteria are outlined for an industry, profession, or job in Section B (Special Evaluation Criteria by Industry, Profession, or Job), the general evaluation criteria shall apply.

**12. Criteria exemptions based on industry, profession, or job**

12.1. For foreigners whose work permit applications fall under the exemptions from industry-specific, profession-specific, or job-specific evaluation criteria outlined in Section B, applications for work permits made within six months of the start date to work for a different employer, or in an industry, profession, or job not specified in Section B, will be evaluated negatively, except in cases of force majeure.

##### C. EVALUATION CRITERIA FOR FOREIGNERS WHO ARE COMPANY PARTNERS

**1. Financial eligibility and employment criteria for foreigners who are company partners**

1.1. For businesses operating under the balance sheet method:

a) In evaluating a work permit application for a foreigner who is opening a new business or becoming a partner in an existing business, the foreigner must have at least 500,000 TL as their share of the capital, and the total paid-up capital of the business they are partnering in must also be at least 500,000 TL. Additionally, the foreigner's shareholding must be at least 20%.

b) In evaluating a work permit application for a foreigner who is opening a new business or becoming a partner in an existing business, the business must employ at least five Turkish citizens. For the initial work permit issued to the foreign partner or business owner, this condition will be explicitly noted. From the start of the seventh month of the permit, the business must employ at least five Turkish citizens every month.

1.2. For foreign partners with a capital share of 100,000 USD or more, the criteria set out in subparagraphs (a) and (b) of paragraph 1 will not apply.

##### Ç. FOREIGNERS EXEMPT FROM EVALUATION CRITERIA

**1. Foreigners exempt from evaluation criteria**

1.1. The following foreigners are exempt from the employment, financial eligibility, and salary criteria when applying for a work permit:

a) Foreigners whose parent or child is a Turkish citizen.

b) Foreigners who have been granted a humanitarian residence permit.

c) Foreigners who have been granted a residence permit as victims of human trafficking, or who are benefiting from a victim support program under the Regulation on the Fight Against Human Trafficking and Protection of Victims.

ç) Stateless persons with a Stateless Person Identity Card.

d) Foreigners granted a long-term residence permit.

e) Foreigners who have been married to a Turkish citizen for at least three years.

f) Foreigners who have resided in Türkiye for at least eight years under a work permit, a short-term residence permit, a family residence permit, a student residence permit, a long-term residence permit, a humanitarian residence permit, or a residence permit for victims of human trafficking*. (Effective as of August 3, 2026.)*

g) Foreigners of Turkish descent, as confirmed by the Ministry of Interior or Ministry of Foreign Affairs, or those identified by the General Directorate as suitable under the international labour force policy, who will work in professions reserved for Turkish citizens.

ğ) Citizens of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC).

1.2. Foreigners in the first paragraph must prove their status with documents from public institutions and organizations.

1.3. Being included in the first paragraph does not guarantee the issuance of a work permit for the foreigner.

##### D. OTHER PROVISIONS

**1. Voluntary activities**

1.1. Work permit applications for activities that do not qualify as employment and are only for the purpose of voluntary work will be negatively evaluated.

**2. Transitional provisions**

2.1. For work permit extensions for permits granted before the evaluation criteria came into effect, the evaluation of the extension request may differ under the international labour force policy of the General Directorate. Work Permit Extensions will be evaluated based on the financial eligibility criteria in effect at the time of the initial application.

**3. Execution**

3.1. The criteria outlined in Section A, Article 2 ("Financial Eligibility Criteria") regarding paid-up capital and net sales thresholds, and the capital share threshold in Section C, Article 1 (Foreign Company Partners' Financial Eligibility and Employment Criteria), will come into effect on 01/10/2024, except for the specific thresholds mentioned.

3.2. The implementation of the thresholds for paid-up capital and net sales in Section A, Article 2, and the capital share threshold in Section C, Article 1, will come into effect on 01/01/2025.

3.3. Until 01/01/2025, the following will be considered sufficient for meeting the financial eligibility criteria for work permit applications:

a) The business must have at least 100,000 TL in paid-up capital, at least 800,000 TL in gross sales, or at least 150,000 USD in export volume for the last year.

b) For foreign company partners, a capital share of at least 40,000 TL will be considered sufficient for meeting the financial eligibility criteria.

title: Residence Permit after Graduation - Sabancı University
text:
#### Residence Permit After Graduation

As is known, after your graduation, you must leave Turkey within 10 days after the expiration date of your student residence permit card. However, some of our students wish to stay in Turkey for reasons such as finding a job or continuing their education. To enable these students to stay in Turkey legally without needing to leave the country, all our full-time students who meet the condition of **having graduated within the last 6 months** from the university can apply for a short-term residence permit transition from a student residence permit. In this way, you can get a short-term residence permit for about up to 1 year. We briefly mention the general information on the issue here. However, you can call 157 for the details and the best answers.

Note: We have been informed that if students' current residence permits extend beyond their graduation date, these permits will remain active. However, we do not know how long they will remain active, and it is generally understood that residence permits may be canceled within 90 days after graduation. Therefore, we recommend that you apply for a short-term residence permit 5 days before your graduation date, which you can find out from student resources. You can check the status of your permit by calling 157.

To apply for this type of permit, if your current card has not expired, you can apply for a transfer on the official website a couple of days before your official graduation date. However, if your card has expired and the period you have stayed in the country does not exceed 10 days, you may need to make a first application for a short-term residence permit and select 'graduation' as the reason. The important thing here is to apply within 6 months after graduation. Additionally, if you apply after your residence permit card has expired and this exceeds 10 days, the Directorate General of Migration Management may negatively evaluate your application or require you to leave and re-enter Turkey. Therefore, the expiration date of your current card and your graduation dates are very important in your application. This is why we recommend applying for this type of permit before your current card expires.

**Application link for the transfer application to a short-term residence permit:**https://e-ikamet.goc.gov.tr/Ikamet/UzatmaGecisGiris/GecisBasvuru

This situation DOES NOT apply to the students who cancel their registration, the students who freeze their registration, the students who have a hold, or the students who have dismissal from the university.

*After completing the online application form, the graduate student must go to their appointment with the following documents (Additional documents may be requested from you if deemed necessary.):*

- Online application form
- Photocopy of passport ID and entry stamp pages to Turkey
- Original passport
- Copy of old residence permit card
- 4 biometric photographs. (It is recommended that the photo size be 4 x 6 and have a white background. They may not accept biometric photos in smaller sizes.)
- Photocopy of temporary graduation certificate or diploma. This document should be obtained from the Student Resources.
- Residence Certificate (Yerleşim Yeri Belgesi). If your address is not registered in the e-devlet address system, you can register your address by going to the Immigration Office with your valid residence permit card before it expires.
- Health insurance (Private, full 1 year, obtained from Turkey)
- Residence permit fee and card fee. The residence permit fee and card fee are also written on the application document that is printed out as a result of the online application. After paying it to the tax office, the student has to add the receipt to the application file as well.
- UETS Code Copy

You can complete these documents and submit them to the Immigration Office on your appointment day.

- You can learn your graduation date **only** from the Student Resources.

If you are no longer a Sabancı University student, as the IRO and the University, we are not responsible for the residence permit applications after your graduation.

**If you are going to continue your education at Sabancı or another university after graduation:**

Students who will graduate from our university from a program and continue their education with another program from our university, must make a first-time application and apply for a student residence permit and prepare extension documents within 20 days after their graduation. They must attach the student certificate of the department that they are newly registered with and use their graduation certificate taken from e-devlet. Even if your card has months until its expiry, this step is required for the ones who upgrade their education level (from undergrad to grad).

If you will continue your education out of Sabancı, the steps are the same but you must get your own university's help in this regard.

title: Residence Permit for Exchange Students - Sabancı University
text:
#### Residence Permit Application for

<u>Exchange Students</u>
**Why Residence Permit?**

<sup>Exchange Students who are enrolled in an academic program in Turkey for 3 months or longer are obliged to acquire a short-term residence permit as per the Law on Foreigners and International Protection. The Residence Permit gives you the right to stay in Turkey during your study period.</sup>

<sup>You must apply for a short term residence permit **before the expiry of your visa, visa exemption period, or residence permit card** and your passport must be valid at least 60 days beyond the requested ending date of residence permit. To do this**, you must enter Turkey with your passport**; you need to complete the necessary documents, submit fingerprints, make an online residence permit application and submit your documents to International Relations Office.</sup>

<sup>Disclaimer</sup>

1. <sup>An application can be only made after entering Turkey. Residence permit applications made from abroad are invalid.</sup>
2. <sup>It is not recommended to leave Turkey before obtaining the residence permit card. Departing from Turkey before the residence permit evaluation may result in rejection.</sup>
3. <sup>Please make sure all required documents are complete before submitting your online application. Files with missing documents are not accepted by the Immigration Office.</sup>
4. <sup>The Immigration Office reserves the right to request additional documents and to reject applications. Our university only guides you on how to apply and submits your files to the Immigration Office on your behalf. The initiation, evaluation, and approval of the process are entirely the responsibility of the Directorate General of Migration Management. This matter is not within the authority of our university.</sup>

#### Application Steps

**Please follow the required steps by the given deadlines, or you may face delays in getting your residence permit card. These dates change monthly, so remember to refresh this page before starting your application.**

#### Step 1: Collect the Required Documents

#### <u>**\*\*\*Collect the Required Documents between 3 - 14 March 2025\*\*\***</u>

| **Document Name** | | **How to get it** |
| 1. Declaration Document | | Download it **<u>here</u>**, fill, print and sign it. |
| 2. Address Proof Document | | If you are staying on campus ) Get your Dorm Address Document from Dorm Management (Building D2) or request it here: suticket.sabanciuniv.edu |
| | | If you are staying off campus get your <u>Rental Agreement</u> under your name (in Turkish ''Kira Sözleşmesi'') <u>Click here to learn more about how to get it.</u> if you are staying off campus and not have a rental agreement get your <u>letter of commitment</u> (in Turkish ''Taahhüt'') <u>Click here to learn more about how to get it.</u> Note: Airbnb platform is not accepted as an address document. Even if you stay at an Airbnb, you must make a rental agreement or taahhütname with the house owner. |
| 3. Passport Copy | | Get a copy of ID page Entry of Turkey stamp page visa page ( if exist ) |
| 4. Biometric Photo | | Get your 4 biometric photos (size 4x6 cm). There is a photo booth available on campus near the bank office |
| 5. Student Certificate | | Get it from Student Resources |
| 6. Online Application Form | | Follow the Step 2 to learn more about how to get it. |
| 7. The receipt Residence Permit Card payment | | Follow the Step 3 to learn more about how to get it. |
| 8. Finger Print | | Follow the Step 4 to learn more about how to get it. |
| 9. Valid Health Insurance for Residence Permit Purpose | | Click here to learn more about how to get it. |

#### Step2: Submit your Online Application and Get Your Online Application Form

**\*\*\*Submit your Online Application between 17-20 March 2025\*\***

You should submit your online application only within the given dates below. Please ensure that you apply before your visa, visa exemption, or residence permit (if applicable) expires.

| **Online Application Dates** |
| 17-20 March |
| **Online Application Link** |
| **https://e-ikamet.goc.gov.tr/Ikamet/OnKayit** |

**Online Application Instructions**

#### Step3: Pay your Application Fee

You must first obtain a tax ID number. Click here to learn how to get it. Only after then, pay it your residence card fee via either Tax Office, Ziraat Bank, Halk Bank, or Vakıf Bank with the 9207-reference code. If you already have a residence permit card before, you can use the old residence card number as a tax number. Please note that the payment of the card fee must be in your name with your tax ID number.

**See below the addresses of the Tax offices:**

- Yakacık D-100 Kuzey Yanyol Caddesi No: 47/A-B Kartal ISTANBUL
- Kadıköy Tax Office: Osmanağa, Halitağa Caddesi No:19, Kadıköy ISTANBUL

Note: The application fee is subject to change annually.

Make sure to have more than 810₺ cash with you when you go to pay. However, you must pay this amount in total since you are a student in Turkey. The personnel might not be able to speak English. Therefore, you can bring this message to anyone, and they will help you:

“Merhaba! Ben SABANCI Universitesinden geliyorum. Yabanci Uyrukluyum. İkamet kart ücreti ödemeye geldim. Yardiminiz icin tesekkurler.” *(Hello! I study at SABANCI University and am a foreigner. I came here to pay my residence card fee. Thank you for your help in advance.)*

If you pay your residence card fee via bank or tax office, please make sure you have a stamp on the receipt. If not, please ask for a stamp (in TR.: Makbuza mühür basar mısınız?)

Never throw away the original payment document as you have to deliver it to the Immigration Office along with other documents, keep the original document. Otherwise, you will have to pay again

#### Step 4: Get your Finger Print

**\*\*\*Get your Finger Print between 17-20 March 2025\*\***

After completing your online application form, you must go to Pendik Immigration Office or any Immigration Office closest to your location to check your fingerprints and get the criminal record number starting with GI on your application form. You can complete this step by going to the fingerprint section without an appointment with your original passport, student ID card and online application form. You must also have your current residence permit card with you, if you have one.

Note: Even if you have previously provided fingerprints, you need to go to the immigration office to get the GI number. Applications submitted without a GI number will be rejected.

If you have a language problem at the immigration administration, simply show the following Turkish text to the authorities:

“Merhaba. Sabancı Üniversitesi öğrencisiyim. Öğrenci ikameti başvurusu yaptım. Parmak izimi vermek istiyorum.”

*(Hello. I am a Sabancı University student. I applied for a student residence permit. I want to give my fingerprint.)*

| Finger Print Location | Working Hours |
| Pendik Immigration Office: Doğu, Nevbahar Sk No:2, 34890 Pendik/İstanbul Click here to see on Google Map | 9 am to 5 pm between Monday to Friday |

Necessary documents you need to take it with you:

1. Original Passport
2. Student ID Card
3. Residence Permit Online Application Form

#### Step 5: Book an Appointment and submit your documents to IRO

After applying online and checking your fingerprints, you are expected to bring your documents to the IRO by the given date. Your file must contain the necessary documents for your application.

📢❗🚨 Before submitting your file to us, you must obtain approval from the IRO because we cannot accept your file if there are missing documents. To ensure that your file contains no missing documents, you need to send all your scanned documents to irolegal@sabanciuniv.edu After we confirm that your documents are complete, you can make an appointment to bring the documents to the office.

| **Book an Appointment** |
| https://calendly.com/irolegalsabanci/legal-procedures |
| **Submit Location** |
| Room 1168 @ Sabancı Business School |

#### Step 6: Tracking your Residence Permit Card

**\*\*\*Submit your all documents to IRO between 21st March 2025\*\***

After you submit your documents to IRO, we will deliver your file to the Istanbul Provincial Immigration Administration. The evaluation result will be delivered to the student within 30-90 days via email/SMS and Immigration Office website https://e-ikamet.goc.gov.tr/Ikamet/DevamEdenBasvuruGiris

The authority to evaluate and announce results lies with the Directorate General of Migration Management. The IRO does not receive application results. Therefore, we recommend regularly checking the website for updates.

It may take up to 90 days for your application to be approved and for your cards to be prepared. Your cards will be sent to the addresses listed on the address document you provided in your application. Tracking the cards is the student's personal responsibility.

If you provided Sabancı University Tuzla Campus as your address in your residence permit application form, your card will be sent to the Communication Center on campus. You will be notified by the Communication Center once your card arrives.

After receiving your card, please don't forget to send a copy to irolegal@sabanciuniv.edu and studentinfo@sabanciuniv.edu.

title: Document for Address Declaration - Hacettepe
text:
Document for Address Declaration

To declare your address, you need to provide one of the following documents:

- A copy of your property deed if you are staying in your own house
- For extension applications, a certificate of residence and a utility bill (electricity, natural gas, water) under your name.
- If you rent a house, a notarized copy of the rental agreement.
- If you are staying in a hotel or similar accommodation, proof of your stay and a receipt showing payment for the period of stay.
- If you are staying in a student dormitory, you need to provide a document proving that you are staying there. If the document does not have a barcode or QR code, you also need to provide an authorized signatory list of the dormitory.
- If you are staying with a sponsor, you need to provide a notarized commitment letter from the person you are staying with. If the sponsor is married, you also need to provide a notarized commitment letter from their spouse. The sponsor must be a legal resident of Türkiye.

title: Visa and Residence Permit FAQ - Sabancı University
text:
## Visa and Residence Permit

Find out more about the general, specific and requirements for visa and residence permit process.

If you come from countries that require a visa to enter Turkey, you can apply for the relevant visa with your acceptance letter. If you still have any difficulties, you can always contact us. Please keep in mind that a student visa is not a requirement for your registration. You can come with a tourist or any other type of visa. If there is visa exemption between your country and Turkey, you do not need to get any kind of visa. For more information click Visa requirement page.

From the moment you enroll at Sabancı University, our Legal Team will guide you through the residence permit application process by organizing informative webinars and sending detailed emails. Don’t worry—our professional support team will be by your side throughout the entire process, handling document submission and follow-up on your behalf. The residence permit application process begins after you arrive in Turkey and complete your enrollment at our university. However, you will be informed in advance about the required documents to ensure you are well-prepared.

Search for your question at the main search page, browse other question categories or contact us.
